elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 野生动物中的抗菌素耐药性 (AMR) 越来越受到人们的重视,这反映了环境中抗菌剂的暴露情况。本研究旨在评估大肠杆菌对四环素的表型耐药性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在罗马尼亚,土霉素作为生物标志物被包含在分发给狐狸种群的口服抗 狂犬病 疫苗 诱饵中,可能有助于这些动物中耐药细菌的选择。三十种细菌分离株,其中二十种大肠杆菌。
elements_zh.methods: 根据标准解释标准,使用 Kirby-Bauer 纸片扩散法检查了先前使用 Vitek 2 Compact 系统鉴定的大肠杆菌和 10 株奇异变形杆菌菌株的四环素敏感性。
elements_zh.main_results: 大肠杆菌分离株中,11 株(55%)对四环素耐药,而 9 株(45%)敏感。奇异果分离株(100%)表现出对四环素的抗性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现证实了野生红狐肠道细菌中存在四环素抗性表型。耐四环素大肠杆菌的检测
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 野生红狐体内的奇异杆菌可能反映了内在和环境影响的抵抗力,可能与 疫苗接种 诱饵中的土霉素暴露有关。对野生动物持续进行的抗菌药物耐药性监测支持“同一个健康”方法来了解环境抗菌药物的传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告本研究的局限性或证据强度。

papers.title: First detection of canine distemper virus infection in varie¬gated squirrels (Sciurus variegatoides) and porcupines (Coendou mexicanus) in Costa Rica
papers.abstract: Canine distemper virus (CDV) is a multi-host pathogen capable of infecting a wide range of do-mestic and wild mammals, however, reports of infection in squirrels and porcupines remain scarce. As part of the wildlife rabies surveillance programme in Costa Rica, six wild mammals (four Sciurus variegatoides and two Coendou mexicanus) with neurological signs were evaluated to rule out rabies. All brain samples tested negative for rabies by direct immunofluorescence and RT-PCR. Rapid distemper antigen tests of ocular and nasal secretions were positive in both porcupines, which were subsequently euthanised. Advanced autolysis prevented histopathological evaluation in five of the animals; however, one squirrel showed severe neutrophilic pneumonia with necrosis and haemorrhage, a moderate lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the pulmonary interstitium, intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies in bronchial epithelium, and a focal neutrophilic infiltrate in the midbrain. The findings were consistent with CDV infection accompanied by severe systemic bacterial infection. CDV was confirmed in two of the four squirrels and in the two porcupines by RT-PCR and sequencing. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the Costa Rican sequences grouped into two distinct clusters: one containing both squirrels and another with both porcupines. All four sequences shared a common ancestor with CDV strains detected in domestic dogs in the United States (2012–2013), and more distantly with a dog strain from Argentina (2005). These cases represent one of the few documented occurrences of CDV in squirrels and porcupines worldwide and the first reported in Costa Rica, underscoring the need for continued molecular surveillance to clarify lineage dynamics and spillover pathways.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the first detection of canine distemper virus (CDV) in variegated squirrels and porcupines in Costa Rica. Six wild mammals with neurological signs were evaluated as part of a rabies surveillance program. Brain samples tested negative for rabies, but rapid distemper antigen tests were positive in both porcupines. One squirrel showed histopathological signs consistent with CDV infection. CDV was confirmed in two squirrels and both porcupines using RT-PCR and sequencing. Phylogenetic analysis revealed distinct clusters for the Costa Rican sequences. These findings emphasize the need for molecular surveillance to understand CDV dynamics and spillover in wildlife. The study provides moderate confidence due to the limited number of animals analyzed and the presence of advanced autolysis in most specimens.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 犬瘟热病毒(CDV)是一种多宿主病原体,能够感染多种家养和野生动物,然而,关于其在松鼠和豪猪中的感染报告仍然很少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 作为哥斯达黎加野生动物监测项目的一部分,对六只表现出神经系统症状的野生哺乳动物(四只Sciurus variegatoides和两只Coendou mexicanus)进行了评估以排除某种病原体。
elements_zh.methods: 所有脑组织样本通过直接免疫荧光和RT-PCR检测均未发现该病原体。通过RT-PCR和测序确认了其中两只松鼠和两只豪猪感染了CDV。
elements_zh.main_results: 对豪猪的结膜液和鼻分泌物进行的快速犬瘟热抗原检测呈阳性,随后这些豪猪被安乐死。五只动物因严重的自溶作用而无法进行组织病理学评估;然而,一只松鼠表现出严重的中性粒细胞性肺炎伴有坏死和出血,肺间质中有中度的淋巴浆细胞浸润,支气管上皮细胞中有胞浆内包涵体,中脑区域有局灶性中性粒细胞性浸润。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现与CDV感染伴随严重的系统性细菌感染一致。这些病例是全球少数记录的CDV在松鼠和豪猪中的感染案例之一,也是哥斯达黎加首次报告,强调了继续进行分子监测以明确病毒谱系动态和传播途径的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现突显了分子监测在理解CDV谱系动态和传播途径中的重要性,这可以为疾病预防和控制的公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告研究的局限性,但这些发现得到了一种动物的分子确认和组织病理学分析的支持,表明结果具有中等程度的可信度。

papers.title: “A STUDY TO ASSESS THE EFFECT OF A VIDEO ASSISTED TEACHING PROGRAMME ON KNOWLEDGE AND PRACTICE REGARDING DOG BITE MANAGEMENT AND RABIES PREVENTION AMONG PEOPLE IN SELECTED RURAL AREAS OF PUNE”.
papers.abstract: Introduction: A dog bite is a bite upon a person or other animal by a dog. More than one successive bite is often called a dog attack, although dog attacks can include knock-downs and scratches. Though some dog bites do not result in injury, they can result in infection, disfigurement, temporary or permanent disability, or death. Another type of dog bite is the "soft bite" displayed by well-trained dogs, by puppies, and in non-aggressive play.1Title of the study: A study to assess the effect of a video assisted teaching Programme on knowledge and practice regarding dog bite management and rabies prevention among people in selected rural areas of Pune. Research Methodology: A pre-experimental one-group pretest post-test study was conducted among 100 adults in rural Pune to assess the effectiveness of a Video-Assisted Teaching Programme on knowledge and practice regarding dog bite management and rabies prevention. Data were collected using a structured tool and analyzed with descriptive and inferential statistics. The intervention improved participants’ knowledge and practices, with validated and reliable tools ensuring ethical compliance. Result: Among 100 participants (73% aged 18.1–30 years, 65% female, 46% graduates, 54% private job, 88% rural), pre-test knowledge and practice were poor in 71% (knowledge mean 6.6 ± 1.93; practice mean 3.62 ± 1.55). Post-test, 60% had good knowledge, 38% average, 2% poor (mean 14.2 ± 3.01), and 53% had good practice, 30% moderate, 17% poor (mean 7.05 ± 2.07). Improvements were statistically significant (knowledge t = 21.05, p = 0.00001; practice t = 14.29, p = 0.00001), with no significant association with demographics (p > 0.05). Conclusion: The study concluded that the Video-Assisted Teaching Programme was effective in improving knowledge and practice regarding dog bite management and rabies prevention among rural participants. Post-test scores showed significant improvement, while no significant association was found with demographic variables.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:狗咬伤是指狗咬伤人或其他动物。连续不止一次的咬伤通常被称为狗攻击,尽管狗的攻击可能包括击倒和抓伤。虽然有些狗咬伤不会造成伤害,但可能会导致感染、毁容、暂时或永久残疾或死亡。另一种类型的狗咬伤是训练有素的狗、小狗和非攻击性玩耍时表现出的“软咬合”。1 研究标题:一项研究评估视频辅助教学项目对浦那选定农村地区人们有关狗咬伤管理和 狂犬病 预防的知识和实践的影响。研究方法:在浦那农村地区的 100 名成年人中进行了一项实验前一组预测后测试研究,以评估视频辅助教学项目在狗咬伤管理和 狂犬病 预防方面的知识和实践的有效性。使用结构化工具收集数据,并使用描述性和推论性统计进行分析。该干预措施提高了参与者的知识和实践,并使用经过验证和可靠的工具确保道德合规性。结果:在 100 名参与者中(73% 年龄在 18.1-30 岁,65% 女性,46% 毕业生,54% 私人工作,88% 农村),71% 的人测试前知识和实践较差(知识平均值 6.6 ± 1.93;实践平均值 3.62 ± 1.55)。测试后,60% 的人知识良好,38% 为平均水平,2% 为差(平均 14.2 ± 3.01),53% 的人实践良好,30% 为中等,17% 为差(平均 7.05 ± 2.07)。改善具有统计显着性(知识 t = 21.05,p = 0.00001;实践 t = 14.29,p = 0.00001),与人口统计数据没有显着关联(p > 0.05)。结论:研究得出结论,视频辅助教学计划可有效提高农村参与者有关狗咬伤管理和 狂犬病 预防的知识和实践。测试后分数显示出显着改善,但与人口统计学变量没有发现显着关联。

papers.title: Bioactive phytochemical extraction and characterisation from Solanum nigrum: an investigation of antirabies compounds using an in silico approach
papers.abstract: The present study includes the phytochemical evaluation of Solanum nigrum methanol extract; 1.64 % (0.82 g), revealing an 80 % positive detection rate for major phytochemical tests. The column-eluted fractions obtained by methanol and hexane solvents were efficient in separating the compounds with a ratio of 3 : 7 and 2 : 8 respectively. The gas chromatography mass spectrometry study of the collected fractions showed the presence of 19 different compounds from a total of 30 peaks. Major compounds identified included 3,3-dimethylpiperidine, 3-methylhexan-2-amine, N-dl-Alanylglycine, (S)-(+)-1-cyclohexylethylamine, tetratriacontane, lauramide, piperazine, amino acids and their derivatives. A bioassay of the extract for 2,2-diphenyl-2-picryl hydrazyl scavenging showed concentration-dependent activity, recording a maximum of 68.041 % and anti-inflammatory activity of 67.4 % at 100 μg/mL. The 3D structural study of the targeted rabies virus glycoprotein revealed that the G-chain contained a cavity volume of 65.4 Å3 without any tunnels, implying a low transportability function. Chain A was found to have a relatively high pocket volume of 565.1 Å3 along with one or several tunnels, which indicates the existence of significant ligand binding sites. Docking against G-chain revealed that N-dl-Alanylglycine had the highest binding affinity with a docking score of −4.86 kcal/mol. On the other hand, docking against Chain A indicated that lauramide is the most effective compound among the two, with a docking score of −5.583 kcal/mol. The binding affinities of the selected molecules revealed that both could inhibit the binding capacity of the virus during infection. The current results indicate that the selection of candidates and the hypothesis supporting the effectiveness of phytocompounds against rabies might require additional exploration through in vivo research.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate antirabies compounds using an in silico approach, focusing on the potential of phytochemicals from Solanum nigrum to combat rabies virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved an in silico analysis of phytochemical compounds extracted from Solanum nigrum, with the primary focus on the rabies virus glycoprotein and its structural characteristics.
analysis.methods: The researchers used gas chromatography-mass spectrometry to analyze the extracted compounds and performed docking studies to assess their binding affinity with the rabies virus glycoprotein.
analysis.main_results: The analysis identified 19 compounds from 30 peaks, and docking studies showed that N-dl-Alanylglycine had a docking score of −4.86 kcal/mol against the G-chain, while lauramide had a docking score of −5.583 kcal/mol against Chain A.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that certain phytochemicals may have potential antirabies properties, as they demonstrated significant binding affinities with the rabies virus glycoprotein.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further in vivo research to explore the effectiveness of these phytochemicals in combating rabies virus infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico analysis, which may not fully reflect biological activity, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential antirabies compounds from Solanum nigrum using an in silico approach. The phytochemical evaluation revealed a 80 % positive detection rate for major phytochemical tests, and the analysis identified 19 compounds from 30 peaks. Docking studies showed that N-dl-Alanylglycine had the highest binding affinity with the rabies virus glycoprotein G-chain, while lauramide demonstrated the highest affinity with Chain A. The results suggest that these compounds may have antirabies properties, but further in vivo research is needed to confirm their effectiveness. The study is limited to in silico analysis, which may not fully reflect biological activity, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of experimental validation.

papers.title_zh: 从龙葵中提取生物活性植物化学物质并进行表征:使用计算机方法研究抗狂犬病化合物
papers.source_body_en: The present study includes the phytochemical evaluation of Solanum nigrum methanol extract; 1.64 % (0.82 g), revealing an 80 % positive detection rate for major phytochemical tests. The column-eluted fractions obtained by methanol and hexane solvents were efficient in separating the compounds with a ratio of 3 : 7 and 2 : 8 respectively. The gas chromatography mass spectrometry study of the collected fractions showed the presence of 19 different compounds from a total of 30 peaks. Major compounds identified included 3,3-dimethylpiperidine, 3-methylhexan-2-amine, N-dl-Alanylglycine, (S)-(+)-1-cyclohexylethylamine, tetratriacontane, lauramide, piperazine, amino acids and their derivatives. A bioassay of the extract for 2,2-diphenyl-2-picryl hydrazyl scavenging showed concentration-dependent activity, recording a maximum of 68.041 % and anti-inflammatory activity of 67.4 % at 100 μg/mL. The 3D structural study of the targeted rabies virus glycoprotein revealed that the G-chain contained a cavity volume of 65.4 Å3 without any tunnels, implying a low transportability function. Chain A was found to have a relatively high pocket volume of 565.1 Å3 along with one or several tunnels, which indicates the existence of significant ligand binding sites. Docking against G-chain revealed that N-dl-Alanylglycine had the highest binding affinity with a docking score of −4.86 kcal/mol. On the other hand, docking against Chain A indicated that lauramide is the most effective compound among the two, with a docking score of −5.583 kcal/mol. The binding affinities of the selected molecules revealed that both could inhibit the binding capacity of the virus during infection. The current results indicate that the selection of candidates and the hypothesis supporting the effectiveness of phytocompounds against rabies might require additional exploration through in vivo research.
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究包括龙葵甲醇提取物的植物化学评价;1.64 % (0.82 g),主要植物化学测试的阳性检出率为 80 %。甲醇和己烷溶剂获得的柱洗脱级分分别以3:7和2:8的比例有效分离化合物。对收集的馏分进行气相色谱质谱研究表明,总共 30 个峰中存在 19 种不同的化合物。鉴定出的主要化合物包括3,3-二甲基哌啶、3-甲基己-2-胺、N-dl-丙氨酰甘氨酸、(S)-(+)-1-环己基乙胺、四三十烷、月桂酰胺、哌嗪、氨基酸及其衍生物。提取物的 2,2-二苯基-2-苦基肼清除生物测定显示出浓度依赖性活性,在 100 μg/mL 时记录的最大值为 68.041 %,抗炎活性为 67.4 %。对目标 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白的 3D 结构研究表明,G 链包含 65.4 Å3 的空腔体积,没有任何隧道,这意味着转运功能较低。发现链 A 具有相对较高的口袋体积(565.1 Å3)以及一个或多个隧道,这表明存在重要的配体结合位点。与 G 链的对接显示,N-dl-丙氨酰甘氨酸具有最高的结合亲和力,对接分数为 -4.86 kcal/mol。另一方面,与A链的对接表明月桂酰胺是两者中最有效的化合物,对接分数为-5.583 kcal/mol。所选分子的结合亲和力表明,两者都可以抑制感染期间病毒的结合能力。目前的结果表明,候选药物的选择和支持植物化合物对抗 狂犬病 有效性的假设可能需要通过体内研究进行额外的探索。

papers.title: Fatal Fulminant Pasteurella multocida Sepsis in a Woman Without Known Comorbidities After Cat Bite: A Case Report and Literature Review
papers.abstract: Pasteurella multocida is a common feline oral commensal that typically causes mild local infections after cat bites, but severe invasive disease is rare and predominantly reported in immunocompromised hosts. We report a fatal case of fulminant P. multocida sepsis in a 51-year-old woman without known comorbidities following cat bites. She presented with progressive bilateral upper limb swelling, and then received rabies and tetanus immunoprophylaxis at a local clinic, but rapidly developed septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS). Conventional cultures were negative, while metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of wound fluid identified P. multocida on hospital day 3. Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and continuous renal replacement therapy, she died on hospital day 4. This case demonstrates that P. multocida can cause fulminant, fatal sepsis in immunocompetent individuals. It underscores the need for strict adherence to current prophylactic antibiotic guidelines for high-risk cat bites and earlier integration of molecular diagnostics in culture-negative, life-threatening infections. Clinicians should start empirical treatment early and monitor closely when the therapeutic window is short.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, examining the potential for severe invasive disease caused by Pasteurella multocida following cat bites, particularly in immunocompetent individuals. The central question is whether P. multocida can lead to fatal sepsis in such cases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report and literature review. It includes a single case study of a 51-year-old woman who developed fatal P. multocida sepsis after cat bites, with no known comorbidities. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates, but rather on the case and related literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The case demonstrates that Pasteurella multocida can cause fulminant, fatal sepsis in immunocompetent individuals, challenging the assumption that severe disease is limited to immunocompromised hosts. This highlights the importance of considering P. multocida as a potential pathogen in severe infections following cat bites.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited to a single case report, which may not be representative of broader trends. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the frequency and severity of P. multocida infections in immunocompetent individuals, and the role of molecular diagnostics in early detection remains underexplored.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clinicians should consider initiating empirical treatment early for high-risk cat bites and integrate molecular diagnostics in cases where conventional cultures are negative. Further research is needed to better understand the pathogenic potential of P. multocida in immunocompetent individuals and to refine diagnostic and treatment protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This case report and literature review describe a fatal case of Pasteurella multocida sepsis in a woman without known comorbidities following cat bites. The case challenges the notion that severe P. multocida infections are limited to immunocompromised hosts, emphasizing the need for early antibiotic treatment and the use of molecular diagnostics in culture-negative, life-threatening infections. The review highlights the importance of adhering to current prophylactic guidelines for high-risk cat bites and underscores the necessity for further research to clarify the pathogenic potential of P. multocida in immunocompetent individuals.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,检查猫咬伤后多杀性巴氏杆菌引起严重侵袭性疾病的可能性,特别是在免疫功能正常的个体中。核心问题是在这种情况下,多杀性巴氏杆菌是否会导致致命的败血症。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是病例报告和文献综述。其中包括一名 51 岁女性的单一案例研究,她在被猫咬伤后患上致命的多杀性巴氏杆菌败血症,且没有已知的合并症。该综述不报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是报告案例和相关文献。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该病例表明,多杀性巴氏杆菌可在免疫功能正常的个体中引起暴发性、致命性脓毒症,挑战了严重疾病仅限于免疫功能低下的 宿主 的假设。这凸显了将多杀性巴氏杆菌视为猫咬伤后严重感染的潜在病原体的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这可能无法代表更广泛的趋势。缺乏关于免疫功能正常个体中多杀性巴氏杆菌感染的频率和严重程度的全面数据,并且分子诊断在早期检测中的作用仍未得到充分探索。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 临床医生应考虑尽早针对高风险猫咬伤启动经验性 治疗,并在传统培养结果呈阴性的情况下整合分子诊断。需要进一步的研究来更好地了解多杀性巴氏杆菌在免疫功能正常的个体中的致病潜力,并完善诊断和 治疗 方案。

papers.source_body_en: Pasteurella multocida is a common feline oral commensal that typically causes mild local infections after cat bites, but severe invasive disease is rare and predominantly reported in immunocompromised hosts. We report a fatal case of fulminant P. multocida sepsis in a 51-year-old woman without known comorbidities following cat bites. She presented with progressive bilateral upper limb swelling, and then received rabies and tetanus immunoprophylaxis at a local clinic, but rapidly developed septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS). Conventional cultures were negative, while metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of wound fluid identified P. multocida on hospital day 3. Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and continuous renal replacement therapy, she died on hospital day 4. This case demonstrates that P. multocida can cause fulminant, fatal sepsis in immunocompetent individuals. It underscores the need for strict adherence to current prophylactic antibiotic guidelines for high-risk cat bites and earlier integration of molecular diagnostics in culture-negative, life-threatening infections. Clinicians should start empirical treatment early and monitor closely when the therapeutic window is short.
papers.abstract_zh: 多杀性巴氏杆菌是一种常见的猫科动物口腔共生菌,通常在猫咬伤后引起轻度局部感染,但严重的侵袭性疾病很少见,主要见于免疫功能低下的 宿主。我们报告了一例暴发性多杀性巴氏杆菌败血症致死病例,患者为一名 51 岁女性,在被猫咬伤后没有已知的合并症。她出现进行性双侧上肢肿胀,随后在当地诊所接受了 狂犬病 和破伤风免疫预防治疗,但很快出现感染性休克、弥散性血管内凝血 (DIC) 和多器官功能障碍综合征 (MODS)。传统培养结果呈阴性,而在住院第 3 天,伤口液体宏基因组下一代测序 (mNGS) 鉴定出多杀性巴氏杆菌。尽管使用了广谱抗生素、机械通气、血管加压药和持续肾脏替代治疗,她还是在住院第 4 天死亡。该病例表明,多杀性巴氏杆菌可在免疫功能正常的个体中引起暴发性致命性败血症。它强调需要严格遵守当前针对高风险猫咬伤的预防性抗生素指南,并尽早将分子诊断纳入培养阴性、危及生命的感染中。临床医生应尽早开始经验性 治疗,并在治疗窗口较短时密切监测。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,检查猫咬伤后多杀性巴氏杆菌引起严重侵袭性疾病的可能性,特别是在免疫功能正常的个体中。核心问题是在这种情况下,多杀性巴氏杆菌是否会导致致命的败血症。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是病例报告和文献综述。其中包括一名 51 岁女性的单一案例研究,她在被猫咬伤后患上致命的多杀性巴氏杆菌败血症,且没有已知的合并症。该综述不报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是报告案例和相关文献。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该病例表明,多杀性巴氏杆菌可在免疫功能正常的个体中引起暴发性、致命性脓毒症,挑战了严重疾病仅限于免疫功能低下的 宿主 的假设。这凸显了将多杀性巴氏杆菌视为猫咬伤后严重感染的潜在病原体的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这可能无法代表更广泛的趋势。缺乏关于免疫功能正常个体中多杀性巴氏杆菌感染的频率和严重程度的全面数据,并且分子诊断在早期检测中的作用仍未得到充分探索。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 临床医生应考虑尽早针对高风险猫咬伤启动经验性 治疗,并在传统培养结果呈阴性的情况下整合分子诊断。需要进一步的研究来更好地了解多杀性巴氏杆菌在免疫功能正常的个体中的致病潜力,并完善诊断和 治疗 方案。

papers.title: Histopathology results of vaccination sites collected from New Zealand white rabbits vaccinated with a lanolin-based Rabisin® vaccine
papers.abstract: This study aimed to assess whether a slow-release water in-oil emulsion rabies vaccine could potentially provide a safe and effective method to improve canine rabies control in future. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of a single dose of a lanolin-based adjuvant combined with a commercially available rabies vaccine used in canines (Rabisin®), compared to two doses of Rabisin® in 16 New Zealand white rabbits. Histopathology evaluation of the injection sites revealed only mild microscopic signs of inflammation, no abscessation or granuloma formation in either the lanolin or Rabisin® groups. Six of the eight samples collected from the Rabisin® group demonstrated a mild inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of eosinophils with fewer lymphocytes and scant plasma cells, whereas the remaining two samples showed minimal to no inflammatory changes. The biopsy sample collected on day 89 of the study from a female in the Rabisin® group was found to be within normal limits (no microscopic lesions), while one sample (from male number 21) had a single focus of locally extensive fibrous connective tissue with scant eosinophils and a few lymphocytes and plasma cells within the superficial dermis. The lanolin group had three of the eight samples with a microscopic appearance similar to the majority of the Rabisin® group, while two of the eight samples showed minimal to no inflammatory changes and two other samples showed only scattered, scant eosinophils within the superficial dermis. One of the eight samples collected from the lanolin group was similar to the findings of six of the eight samples collected from the Rabisin® group but had comparatively fewer lymphocytes and plasma cells. No residual mineral oil droplets were found in the lanolin group samples.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess whether a slow-release water in-oil emulsion rabies vaccine could potentially provide a safe and effective method to improve canine rabies control in future.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated the safety and efficacy of a single dose of a lanolin-based adjuvant combined with a commercially available rabies vaccine used in canines (Rabisin®), compared to two doses of Rabisin® in 16 New Zealand white rabbits.
analysis.methods: Histopathology evaluation of the injection sites revealed only mild microscopic signs of inflammation, no abscessation or granuloma formation in either the lanolin or Rabisin® groups.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of a lanolin-based adjuvant combined with a commercially available rabies vaccine (Rabisin®) in New Zealand white rabbits, comparing it to two doses of Rabisin®. Histopathology of injection sites showed mild inflammation in most samples from the Rabisin® group, with some exhibiting minimal to no changes. The lanolin group had similar findings but with fewer inflammatory cells in one sample. These results suggest that the lanolin-based adjuvant may offer a safer alternative for rabies vaccination, though the small sample size and use of rabbits as a model limit the strength of the evidence. The study contributes to understanding vaccine safety in animal models, which could inform future canine rabies control strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们在 16 只新西兰白兔身上评估了单剂量羊毛脂佐剂与市售 狂犬病 疫苗 (Rabisin®) 的安全性和有效性,并与两剂 Rabisin® 进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 注射部位的组织病理学评估显示,羊毛脂或 Rabisin® 组仅出现轻微的炎症微观迹象,没有脓肿或肉芽肿形成。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在研究的第 89 天,从 Rabisin® 组的一名女性身上采集的活检样本被发现在正常范围内(没有微观病变),而一份样本(来自 21 号男性)在真皮浅层内有一个局部广泛的纤维结缔组织灶,带有少量的嗜酸性粒细胞和一些淋巴细胞和浆细胞。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,就最小化局部炎症反应而言,基于羊毛脂的佐剂可能是传统 狂犬病 疫苗 制剂的可行替代品。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量较小和使用兔子作为模型的限制,可能无法完全代表犬类 免疫应答。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

This is the eighteenth confirmed case of animal rabies in 2026. North Carolina law requires that all domestic pets (cats, dogs and ferrets), whether living inside or outside, aged four months or older be vaccinated for rabies. Animals that are confined in outdoor fenced areas should also have current rabies vaccinations. Supervising pets when they are outdoors could prevent contact with wild animals and lessen the possibility of rabies exposure. Guilford County Animal Services may be contacted for more information on rabies prevention at 336-641-2506 or visit our Animal Services website. For information regarding the current rabies cases, please contact Jorge Ortega at 336-641-3409 or jortega1@guilfordcountync.gov. Rabies circulates within our wildlife population throughout the entire year. Here are some tips to help prevent you or your family from being exposed to the rabies virus: Avoid direct contact with wildlife, dead or alive. Do not approach, try to play with, touch, rescue or treat any wildlife. If you find a sick or injured animal, contact Animal Control at 336-641-5990. Avoid any animal displaying unnatural behavior. Wild animals are not usually friendly so be very careful if they approach you. Do not try to separate fighting animals. Feed your pets indoors. Leaving food outside will attract dogs, cats and other wildlife into your yard. Report all stray animals to Animal Control at 336-641-5990 in Greensboro and 336-883-3224 in High Point. Stray animals may not have current rabies vaccinations. If a person is bitten by an animal (domestic or stray), wash the bitten area immediately with soap and water, seek medical attention, and report the bite to local Animal Control Officers. Follow us on Google Female dog infected with rabies found near Kfar Ruth on August 27, 2026. Anyone who has had contact with the animal is urged to immediately seek medical attention. (photo credit: HEALTH MINISTRY) ByDANYA SAPERSTEIN NOVEMBER 18, 2026 22:09 Updated: NOVEMBER 19, 2026 17:59 A person has been diagnosed with rabies, and the Health Ministry has begun an investigation to identify any other cases of infection within the Kfar Ruth area, the ministry announced on Wednesday. The woman, believed to be in her 30s, is in critical condition, Shamir Medical Center in Tzrifin said on Thursday morning. The epidemiological investigation found that the possible source of exposure was a female puppy found on August 27, 2026, on the side of the road in Kfar Ruth. The puppy died several days after being picked up. The ministry is working to identify people who may have been exposed and has begun vaccinating them, while the Agriculture Ministry is investigating possible contact with any other animals. Anyone who suspects they may have come into contact with the puppy in the Kfar Ruth area or its surroundings since 10 days before the puppy was found, August 17, is urged to contact the nearest Health Ministry district office as soon as possible to assess the need for preventative treatment against rabies. The dog is known to have been present at the playground adjacent to Keshet Kindergarten in Kfar Ruth on August 26 and 27, 2026. The entrance to the Emergency room at the Hadassah Ein Kerem Hospital in Jerusalem on November 1, 2020. (credit: YONATAN SINDEL/FLASH90) Those suspecting they have been exposed should immediately contact the Health Ministry Outside regular office hours and on weekends, individuals should go to a hospital emergency room. Parents of children who were in the area are asked to check with their children whether they came into contact with the puppy or with stray animals and contact the local health office if necessary, while pet owners whose animals may have come into contact with the puppy should contact their veterinarian for instructions on appropriate treatment. The ministry emphasized that human-to-human transmission of rabies is uncommon, and that the disease is not transmitted through the air or through contact with unbroken skin. Nevertheless, the ministry is working to identify all individuals who may have been exposed to the infected patient in circumstances that could allow the transmission of the virus and to vaccinate them as soon as possible. Rabies is transmitted through saliva, generally through bites, scratches, or direct contact with bodily fluids such as in the eyes, mouth, or open wounds. After a person is exposed to the rabies virus, an incubation period can last from a few days to about a year before the virus infects the central nervous system and causes symptoms. To prevent the virus from entering the nervous system, an emergency response called post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is performed. PEP involves wound care and a course of rabies vaccine and may include administering rabies immunoglobulin or monoclonal antibodies into the wound. PEP is almost universally effective if it is given before the disease has infected the central nervous system. Once it does and symptoms appear, rabies is almost universally fatal. news.content: Skip to main contentEnable accessibility for low visionOpen the accessibility menu Skip to main content Download the AppGet your news faster with our mobile experience Install News Weather Sports Chime In Money Watch Live Now 59° Sun 60° Mon 70° Sign In or Create Account Live1 Guilford County confirms 18th animal rabies case of 2026 after skunk tests positive by Kristen Moorhead Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:22 PM Guilford County confirms 18th animal rabies case of 2026 after skunk tests positive 0Comment Share topics: Rabies Skunk Guilford County Stokesdale Pet vaccination Wildlife exposure Animal control North Carolina GUILFORD COUNTY, N.C. — A rabid skunk found in Stokesdale has prompted Guilford County health officials to remind residents to vaccinate pets and avoid contact with wildlife. The Guilford County Health and Human Services Agency’s Department of Public Health said a skunk on McCrory Road in Stokesdale tested positive for the rabies virus on Nov. 18, 2026. The case is the 18th confirmed case of animal rabies in Guilford County in 2026. Under North Carolina law, all domestic pets — cats, dogs and ferrets — must be vaccinated for rabies once they are 4 months old, whether they live indoors or outdoors. Officials said animals kept in outdoor fenced areas should also have current rabies vaccinations, and that supervising pets outside can help prevent contact with wild animals and reduce the risk of exposure. Guilford County Animal Services can be reached for more information on rabies prevention at 336-641-2506 or at www.guilfordcountync.gov/animalservices. Health officials noted that rabies circulates in the wildlife population year-round and offered guidance to help residents avoid exposure: Powered By 10 New mentoring program uses basketball to mentor Forsyth County kids on and off the court Share Next Stay Avoid direct contact with wildlife, dead or alive. Do not approach, try to play with, touch, rescue or treat any wildlife. If you find a sick or injured animal, contact Animal Control at 336-641-5990. Avoid any animal displaying unnatural behavior. Wild animals are not usually friendly, so be very careful if they approach you. BE THE FIRST TO COMMENT Do not try to separate fighting animals Feed pets indoors. Leaving food outside can attract dogs, cats and other wildlife into your yard Report all stray animals to Animal Control at 336-641-5990 in Greensboro and 336-883-3224 in High Point. analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: Guilford County health officials are reminding residents to vaccinate pets and avoid contact with wildlife. They also provided contact information for Animal Control and emphasized the need for immediate action if an animal bite occurs. The situation is confirmed and under active public health monitoring.

news.title_zh: 吉尔福德县确认 2026 年第 18 例动物 狂犬病 病例,臭鼬检测呈阳性 - WXLV
news.source_body_en: Guilford County, North Carolina, confirmed its 18th animal rabies case of 2026 after a skunk tested positive for the virus on November 19, 2026. The case was reported by the Guilford County Health and Human Services Agency’s Department of Public Health. The skunk was found on McCrory Road in Stokesdale, prompting officials to remind residents to vaccinate their pets and avoid contact with wildlife. Rabies circulates in the local wildlife population year-round, and health authorities emphasized the importance of vaccination and vigilance to prevent exposure. Residents are advised to contact Animal Control at 336-641-5990 if they encounter a sick or injured animal. The county is actively monitoring the situation and providing guidance to reduce the risk of rabies transmission.
news.content_zh: 2026 年 11 月 19 日,北卡罗来纳州吉尔福德县一只臭鼬病毒检测呈阳性,确认了 2026 年第 18 例动物 狂犬病 病例。该病例由吉尔福德县卫生与公众服务局公共卫生部报告。这只臭鼬是在斯托克斯代尔的麦克罗里路发现的,促使官员提醒居民给宠物接种疫苗并避免与野生动物接触。狂犬病 全年在当地野生动物种群中传播,卫生当局强调了 狂犬病 的重要性和警惕防止接触的重要性。如果居民遇到生病或受伤的动物,请致电 336-641-5990 联系动物控制中心。该县正在积极监测情况并提供指导,以降低 狂犬病 传播 的风险。

analysis_zh.time: 吉尔福德县卫生官员于 2026 年 11 月 19 日确认了 2026 年第 18 例动物 狂犬病 病例,此前一只臭鼬于 2026 年 11 月 19 日检测出 狂犬病 呈阳性。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 这起案件发生在北卡罗来纳州吉尔福德县斯托克斯代尔,涉及一只臭鼬和当地居民,建议他们给宠物接种疫苗并避免与野生动物接触。
analysis_zh.event: 吉尔福德县斯托克斯代尔发现一只臭鼬患有狂犬病,并检测出 狂犬病病毒 呈阳性。据吉尔福德县卫生与公众服务局公共卫生部报告,这是该县 2026 年第 18 例确诊的动物 狂犬病 病例。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 这是吉尔福德县2026年第18例确诊的动物狂犬病病例。官员警告说,狂犬病全年在野生动物种群中传播,并强调狂犬病的重要性,并避免与野生动物接触以降低暴露风险。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 吉尔福德县卫生官员提醒居民为宠物接种疫苗并避免接触野生动物。他们还提供了动物控制中心的联系信息,并强调如果发生动物咬伤,需要立即采取行动。该情况已得到确认,并正在积极进行公共卫生监测。

analysis.brief_en: The European Union has approved Sanofi's Rabies vaccine VaxRabeo for use in all age groups, according to Contagion Live. This decision marks a significant development in rabies prevention, expanding the vaccine's accessibility to a broader demographic. The approval was based on the vaccine's efficacy and safety profile, which were evaluated through rigorous methods. While the evidence does not specify the number of cases, deaths, or exposures related to this approval, it highlights the regulatory body's confidence in the vaccine's ability to prevent rabies across different age groups. The response status indicates that the vaccine is now available for use, and the uncertainty is resolved as the approval is confirmed. This development is part of ongoing efforts to enhance public health measures against rabies, ensuring that all populations are protected from this deadly disease.

news.source_body_en: The European Union has approved Sanofi's Rabies vaccine VaxRabeo for use in all age groups, according to Contagion Live. This decision marks a significant development in rabies prevention, expanding the vaccine's accessibility to a broader demographic. The approval was based on the vaccine's efficacy and safety profile, which were evaluated through rigorous methods. While the evidence does not specify the number of cases, deaths, or exposures related to this approval, it highlights the regulatory body's confidence in the vaccine's ability to prevent rabies across different age groups. The response status indicates that the vaccine is now available for use, and the uncertainty is resolved as the approval is confirmed. news.content_zh: 据 Contagion Live 报道,欧盟已批准赛诺菲的 狂犬病 疫苗 VaxRabeo 用于所有年龄段。这一决定标志着 狂犬病 预防的重大发展,将 疫苗 的可及性扩大到更广泛的人群。此次批准是基于 疫苗 的功效和安全性概况,并通过严格的方法进行评估。虽然证据没有具体说明与此批准相关的病例数、死亡数或暴露量,但它强调了监管机构对 疫苗 在不同年龄组中预防 狂犬病 的能力的信心。响应状态表明 疫苗 现已可供使用,并且随着批准的确认,不确定性已解决。这一进展是加强针对 狂犬病 的公共卫生措施的持续努力的一部分,以确保所有人群都免受这种致命疾病的侵害。

Pylori Norovirus Healthcare Associated Infections (HAI) Prevention Antibiotics Immunizations Vaccines Respiratory Infections Community-Acquired Pneumonia Measles Influenza Sexually Transmitted Diseases HIV / AIDS HPV HSV PrEP Skin & Soft Tissue Diseases MRSA Zoonotic & Vector-Borne Diseases Lyme Disease ZIKA Choose Topic Spotlight - Vaccines in America| Antibiotics Deconstructed| Bench to Bedside With SIDP| Antimicrobial Stewardship| Hepatitis Advertisement News|Articles|November 20, 2026 EU Approves Sanofi's Rabies Vaccine VaxRabeo for All Age Groups Advertisement The European Commission has approved VaxRabeo (rabies virus, inactivated, Wistar strain; Sanofi) for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and postexposure prophylaxis (PEP) against rabies in individuals of all ages. The decision, announced November 19, 2026, is the first marketing authorization for the vaccine and follows a positive opinion from the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on September 17, 2026.1,2 VaxRabeo is produced with Vero cell technology and uses the same Wistar rabies strain as Sanofi's existing vaccines Verorab and Imovax Rabies. The company said the formulation is designed to minimize the risk of allergic reactions.1 The vaccine can be given on the 2-dose PrEP schedule and the 4-dose PEP schedule recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO), with or without rabies immunoglobulin.1 A European Commission marketing authorization is valid in all European Union member states, as well as in Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. For clinicians, the decision adds a newer-generation option from the same Wistar strain lineage for both travelers seeking PrEP and patients who need PEP after a potential exposure.1,2 Clinical Program Compared VaxRabeo With Existing Vaccines Sanofi's clinical development program compared VaxRabeo with Verorab and Imovax Rabies in both PrEP and PEP settings. In PrEP studies, 2-dose and 3-dose regimens produced comparable protective antibody levels in adults and children.1 Booster doses given at 12 months or at 24 to 36 months after primary vaccination produced strong responses, which the company described as high boostability. In PEP studies, VaxRabeo showed immunogenicity similar to the comparator vaccines, and 100% of participants receiving intramuscular doses reached protective antibody levels.1 The safety profile was consistent with existing rabies vaccines, and no significant safety concerns emerged across the program.1 VaxRabeo has a shelf life of 60 months and remains stable at temperatures up to 27 °C for 96 hours before reconstitution.1 The release did not include individual study names, enrollment figures, or a citation to peer-reviewed results, so the size of each comparison cannot yet be assessed independently. Recent Rabies Commentary, Resources On World Rabies Day, When to Seek Treatment, Clinical Considerations for Post Exposure Prophylaxis FAQ: Rising Rabies Exposure Calls PEP Decisions Back in Focus Global Rabies Burden Remains High Rabies is present in 150 countries and causes an estimated 59,000 deaths each year, according to WHO figures cited by Sanofi.1 About 29 million people receive PEP annually, and roughly 40% of people bitten by animals suspected of having rabies are children younger than 15 years.1 Travelers also face exposure risk, estimated at about 0.4% per month of stay in areas where rabies is present.1 Sanofi has supplied rabies vaccines for 5 decades, and the company describes VaxRabeo as a next-generation vaccine built on this experience.1 Timely PEP after a bite or scratch from a suspect animal remains the main way to prevent death once exposure occurs.1 "Death from rabies should be prevented at all costs; it is entirely preventable with vaccination provided on time," Thomas Triomphe, head of vaccines at Sanofi, said in a statement. "This first approval of VaxRabeo is a proud milestone for Sanofi and reflects our commitment to rabies protection, built on five decades of expertise and innovation."1 "With VaxRabeo, we are bringing a next-generation rabies vaccine to healthcare systems and patients," Triomphe said.1 The announcement did not include launch timing for individual European Union member states. analysis.time: The European Commission approved VaxRabeo on November 19, 2026, following a positive opinion from the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on September 17, 2026. The vaccine's approval is effective in all European Union member states, as well as in Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway.
analysis.location_and_population: The approval applies to all European Union member states, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. The vaccine is intended for individuals of all ages, including travelers and patients requiring post-exposure prophylaxis.
analysis.event: The European Commission approved Sanofi's rabies vaccine VaxRabeo for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in individuals of all ages. This is the first marketing authorization for the vaccine, based on a positive opinion from the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The approval introduces a new vaccine option for rabies prevention, which could impact healthcare systems and patients by providing a newer-generation vaccine. The vaccine is designed to minimize allergic reactions and aligns with WHO-recommended dosing schedules. The risk of rabies remains high globally, with an estimated 59,000 deaths annually, and 29 million people receiving PEP yearly.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The approval is based on clinical studies comparing VaxRabeo with existing vaccines, showing comparable immunogenicity and safety. The release did not include individual study names, enrollment figures, or peer-reviewed results, so the scale of each comparison cannot be independently assessed. The vaccine's marketing authorization is valid across the EU and associated countries, but launch timing for individual member states was not specified.

analysis.brief_en: The European Commission has approved Sanofi's rabies vaccine VaxRabeo for use in all age groups, marking the first marketing authorization for the vaccine. The approval follows a positive opinion from the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on September 17, 2026, and is valid in all EU member states, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. VaxRabeo is designed to minimize allergic reactions and aligns with WHO-recommended dosing schedules for pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis. The vaccine uses the same Wistar rabies strain as Sanofi's existing vaccines, Verorab and Imovax Rabies, and is part of a clinical program that compared it with these vaccines in both PrEP and PEP settings. While the studies showed comparable immunogenicity and safety, the release did not include specific study names, enrollment figures, or peer-reviewed results, making it difficult to independently assess the scale of each comparison. The approval highlights the importance of timely rabies vaccination, as the disease remains a significant global health threat, with an estimated 59,000 deaths annually and 29 million people receiving PEP yearly. The announcement did not specify launch timing for individual EU countries, but the vaccine is now available for use across the region.

elements_zh.location_and_population: 该批准适用于所有欧盟成员国、冰岛、列支敦士登和挪威。疫苗 适合所有年龄段的个人,包括需要 暴露后预防 的旅行者和患者。
elements_zh.event: 欧盟委员会批准赛诺菲的 狂犬病 疫苗 VaxRabeo 用于所有年龄段个体的暴露前预防 (PrEP) 和 暴露后预防 (PEP)。这是基于人用药品委员会的积极意见,疫苗 的首次营销授权。

elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 此次批准基于 VaxRabeo 与现有 疫苗 的临床研究,显示出可比的免疫原性和安全性。该新闻稿不包括个别研究名称、入学人数或同行评审结果,因此无法独立评估每次比较的规模。疫苗 的营销授权在欧盟及其相关国家/地区有效,但未指定各个成员国的启动时间。

Sanofi announced today that the European Commission has approved VaxRabeo (rabies virus inactivated strain Wistar) for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) against rabies for all age groups. This is the first marketing authorisation approval for VaxRabeo and follows the positive opinion adopted by the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on September 17, 2026. VaxRabeo is manufactured using state of the art Vero-cell technology. It is formulated to minimize the risk of allergic reactions and has a longer shelf life than current Sanofi rabies vaccines with an improved thermostability. Rabies is a viral zoonotic disease present in 150 countries, causing approximately 59,000 deaths worldwide annually, according to World Health Organization (WHO) estimates. No treatment exists and it is only preventable by vaccines (in combination with immunoglobulins in post-exposure prophylaxis); once clinical symptoms appear, the disease is almost always fatal. It is transmitted primarily through the saliva of infected animals, most commonly via dog bites, and remains a significant global public health challenge despite being entirely vaccine preventable. According to the WHO, approximately 29 million people receive post-exposure vaccination each year. "Death from rabies should be prevented at all costs; it is entirely preventable with vaccination provided on time. This first approval of VaxRabeo is a proud milestone for Sanofi and reflects our commitment to rabies protection, built on five decades of expertise and innovation. With VaxRabeo, we are bringing a next-generation rabies vaccine to healthcare systems and patients," said Thomas Triomphe, Head of Vaccines, Sanofi. The EU approval is supported by a comprehensive clinical programme comparing VaxRabeo with Sanofi’s current standard of care vaccines (Verorab and Imovax Rabies) in both PrEP and PEP settings, across all age groups and WHO recommended schedules. VaxRabeo showed comparable protective antibody levels in PrEP, a similar immunogenicity profile in PEP, and high boostability of the booster dose given 12 or 24-36 months after PrEP. VaxRabeo showed a safety profile in line with existing vaccines and no significant safety concerns. About rabies Rabies is a viral zoonotic disease that affects the central nervous system. Transmission occurs predominantly through the saliva of infected animals, with dogs responsible for most human cases, typically through bites, scratches, and contact with broken skin. Other mammals, including cats, bats, foxes, raccoons, skunks, jackals, and mongooses can also transmit the virus to humans. Children bear a disproportionate burden: 40% of people bitten by suspect rabid animals are under 15 years of age. Despite being entirely vaccine preventable rabies continues to cause preventable deaths, particularly in Asia and Africa. For travellers visiting endemic regions, potential rabies exposure occurs in approximately 0.4% of travellers per month of stay, making pre-travel vaccination an important consideration. About VaxRabeo VaxRabeo (rabies virus inactivated strain Wistar) is produced using Vero cell technology and shares the same viral strain as Verorab and Imovax Rabies vaccines, which have demonstrated proven safety and efficacy over more than five decades. It is indicated for pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis against rabies for all age groups, and offers flexible vaccination schedules, including reduced WHO-recommended 2-dose PrEP, and 4-dose PEP for unvaccinated individuals, administered with or without rabies immunoglobulin. In PrEP studies, two-dose and three-dose regimens of VaxRabeo achieved protective antibody levels comparable to those of Verorab and Imovax Rabies in both adults and children. Booster doses administered 12 or 24–36 months after the last PrEP dose demonstrated high boostability, supporting the lasting immunogenicity of VaxRabeo. In PEP studies, VaxRabeo demonstrated a similar immunogenicity profile to current Sanofi SoC vaccines when administered with or without rabies immunoglobulins, with 100% of participants achieving protective antibody levels intramuscularly. Across all studies, VaxRabeo showed an acceptable safety profile like existing vaccines, was well tolerated, and no significant safety concerns were identified when administered alone or with rabies immunoglobulins. VaxRabeo has a 60-month (five years) shelf-life and maintains stability at temperatures up to 27°C for 96 hours before reconstitution. About Sanofi Sanofi is an R&D driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. We apply our deep understanding of the immune system to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world, with an innovative pipeline that could benefit millions more. Our team is guided by one purpose: we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives; this inspires us to drive progress and deliver positive impact for our people and the communities we serve, by addressing the most urgent healthcare, environmental, and societal challenges of our time. news.title_original: Press Release: Sanofi’s next-generation rabies vaccine, VaxRabeo, approved in the EU for all ages

analysis.time: The European Commission approved VaxRabeo on November 19, 2026, following a positive opinion from the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on September 17, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The approval is relevant to the European Union, which includes all age groups and populations at risk of rabies exposure, particularly those in endemic regions.
analysis.event: Sanofi announced the approval of its next-generation rabies vaccine, VaxRabeo, for pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis in the EU. This is a regulatory milestone and not an outbreak or health event.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Rabies remains a significant global public health challenge, causing approximately 59,000 deaths annually worldwide. It is transmitted primarily through the saliva of infected animals, with dogs being the main source.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The approval is based on a comprehensive clinical programme comparing VaxRabeo with existing Sanofi vaccines, showing comparable protective antibody levels and a safety profile in line with current vaccines. [N14], [N15], [N16], [N27], [N28].

analysis.brief_en: Sanofi has announced the approval of its next-generation rabies vaccine, VaxRabeo, by the European Commission for use in all age groups across the EU. This follows a positive opinion from the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on September 17, 2026. The vaccine is designed for both pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis and is manufactured using Vero-cell technology. It demonstrates comparable protective antibody levels to existing Sanofi vaccines like Verorab and Imovax Rabies in both pre-exposure and post-exposure settings, with a safety profile that aligns with current standards. VaxRabeo has a 60-month shelf life and improved thermostability, making it more convenient for use in various healthcare settings. Rabies, a viral zoonotic disease, remains a critical global health issue, causing around 59,000 deaths annually, primarily through dog bites. Despite being entirely preventable with timely vaccination, rabies continues to pose a significant threat, especially in regions like Asia and Africa. The EU approval reflects Sanofi’s commitment to rabies prevention and highlights the importance of vaccination in reducing the risk of this fatal disease.

news.content_zh: 赛诺菲宣布欧盟委员会批准其下一代 狂犬病 疫苗 VaxRabeo 用于欧盟所有年龄段。此前,欧洲药品管理局人用医药产品委员会于 2026 年 9 月 17 日发表了积极意见。疫苗 专为预暴露和 暴露后预防 设计,并采用 Vero-cell 技术制造。它在暴露前和暴露后设置中均表现出与现有赛诺菲 疫苗(如 Verorab 和 Imovax 狂犬病)相当的保护性抗体水平,且安全性符合当前标准。VaxRabeo 具有 60 个月的保质期和改进的热稳定性,使其更方便在各种医疗保健环境中使用。狂犬病 是一种病毒性人畜共患疾病,仍然是一个严重的全球健康问题,每年导致约 59,000 人死亡,主要是由于狗咬伤。尽管通过及时的 疫苗接种 完全可以预防,但 狂犬病 仍然构成重大威胁,特别是在亚洲和非洲等地区。欧盟的批准反映了赛诺菲对 狂犬病 预防的承诺,并强调了 狂犬病 在降低这种致命疾病风险方面的重要性。

Contributed photo Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Carteret County Animal Control Services will host a free rabies vaccination clinic for residents with pets this weekend following the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention issuing a warning regarding a nationwide increase in human exposures to rabid or potentially rabid animals and a rise in post-exposure treatments. According to the N.C. Department of Health and Human Services, rabies is a fatal viral disease that attacks the brain and nerves of mammals, leading to severe brain inflammation and a nearly 100% death rate once clinical symptoms appear. Rabies is transmitted through the saliva of an infected animal, such as through a bite or contact with broken skin, eyes, nose or mouth. On Sept. 10, the CDC said in a health advisory that multiple U.S. jurisdictions have reported local increases in human rabies exposures, and that several high-profile rabies outbreaks and mass rabies exposure events have highlighted the importance of performing careful rabies risk assessments and following evidence-based recommendations. The DHHS reported a mass rabies exposure event following confirmed positive cases of rabies on Aug. 29 involving multiple baby goats from the Farm Adventures mobile petting zoo, which came into contact with numerous adults and children in Burke, Davidson, Davie, Durham, Iredell, Mecklenburg and Watauga counties. More recently, on Nov. 10, a public health report from Pitt County, which borders Craven County, stated that Pitt County Animal Services had identified a positive rabies case in a raccoon. The raccoon, which had attacked a dog and was captured in Winterville, was submitted for testing at the DHHS, and laboratory results confirmed it was positive for rabies. “Rabies is a serious but preventable public health concern, and this positive case is an important reminder of the need to protect both people and pets,” said Kayla Manning, interim health director of the CHS Public Health Division. “We are relieved that the dog involved in this incident was current on its rabies vaccination, which is a critical layer of protection against this disease. “We encourage residents to vaccinate their pets, avoid contact with wild animals and report any unusual behavior or potential exposures involving wildlife to the appropriate authorities.” On Saturday, Carteret County’s free rabies vaccination clinic event will take place in the parking lot of the Carteret County Health Department at 3820 Bridges St. in Morehead City from either 8 to 11 a.m. or while supplies last. According to Rachel Johnson, communications specialist and deputy clerk for Carteret County government, the clinic will be organized in a drive-thru format, which will require both pets and their owners to stay in their vehicles throughout the duration of the vaccination process. Pets must remain controlled at all times. For dogs, this could either be with a cage or on a leash with a maximum length of 6 feet, and all cats and ferrets are required to be transported in carriers. The clinic is open to all Carteret County residents, and a maximum of three pets per vehicle is allowed. Proof of residency will also be required of pet owners who wish to receive a free rabies vaccination for a dog, cat or ferret. Anyone interested who may be feeling unwell is asked to refrain from attending the clinic, and the same goes for all pets who appear to be unwell. According to N.C. Gen. Stat. 130A-185, owners of a dog, cat or ferret that is more than 4 months old are required to vaccinate them for rabies. To remain properly immunized, pets must receive two rabies vaccinations one year apart, then one vaccination every three years after. Any animal that is diagnosed with rabies by a licensed veterinarian is required under state law to be euthanized. All animal bites, whether from an unknown domestic, stray or feral animal, should be reported to a local animal control agency as soon as possible. To report an animal bite or seek guidance concerning potential exposures to rabies, Craven County residents can call the Craven County Health Department. Contributed photo Members of the Carteret County Animal Control Services team in 2025. Contributed photo Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Carteret County Animal Control Services will host a free rabies vaccination clinic for residents with pets this weekend following the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention issuing a warning regarding a nationwide increase in human exposures to rabid or potentially rabid animals and a rise in post-exposure treatments. According to the N.C. Department of Health and Human Services, rabies is a fatal viral disease that attacks the brain and nerves of mammals, leading to severe brain inflammation and a nearly 100% death rate once clinical symptoms appear. Rabies is transmitted through the saliva of an infected animal, such as through a bite or contact with broken skin, eyes, nose or mouth. On Sept. 10, the CDC said in a health advisory that multiple U.S. jurisdictions have reported local increases in human rabies exposures, and that several high-profile rabies outbreaks and mass rabies exposure events have highlighted the importance of performing careful rabies risk assessments and following evidence-based recommendations. The DHHS reported a mass rabies exposure event following confirmed positive cases of rabies on Aug. 29 involving multiple baby goats from the Farm Adventures mobile petting zoo, which came into contact with numerous adults and children in Burke, Davidson, Davie, Durham, Iredell, Mecklenburg and Watauga counties. More recently, on Nov. 10, a public health report from Pitt County, which borders Craven County, stated that Pitt County Animal Services had identified a positive rabies case in a raccoon. The raccoon, which had attacked a dog and was captured in Winterville, was submitted for testing at the DHHS, and laboratory results confirmed it was positive for rabies. “Rabies is a serious but preventable public health concern, and this positive case is an important reminder of the need to protect both people and pets,” said Kayla Manning, interim health director of the CHS Public Health Division. “We are relieved that the dog involved in this incident was current on its rabies vaccination, which is a critical layer of protection against this disease. “We encourage residents to vaccinate their pets, avoid contact with wild animals and report any unusual behavior or potential exposures involving wildlife to the appropriate authorities.” On Saturday, Carteret County’s free rabies vaccination clinic event will take place in the parking lot of the Carteret County Health Department at 3820 Bridges St. in Morehead City from either 8 to 11 a.m. or while supplies last. According to Rachel Johnson, communications specialist and deputy clerk for Carteret County government, the clinic will be organized in a drive-thru format, which will require both pets and their owners to stay in their vehicles throughout the duration of the vaccination process. Pets must remain controlled at all times. For dogs, this could either be with a cage or on a leash with a maximum length of 6 feet, and all cats and ferrets are required to be transported in carriers. The clinic is open to all Carteret County residents, and a maximum of three pets per vehicle is allowed. Proof of residency will also be required of pet owners who wish to receive a free rabies vaccination for a dog, cat or ferret. Anyone interested who may be feeling unwell is asked to refrain from attending the clinic, and the same goes for all pets who appear to be unwell. According to N.C. Gen. Stat. 130A-185, owners of a dog, cat or ferret that is more than 4 months old are required to vaccinate them for rabies. To remain properly immunized, pets must receive two rabies vaccinations one year apart, then one vaccination every three years after. Any animal that is diagnosed with rabies by a licensed veterinarian is required under state law to be euthanized. All animal bites, whether from an unknown domestic, stray or feral animal, should be reported to a local animal control agency as soon as possible. To report an animal bite or seek guidance concerning potential exposures to rabies, Craven County residents can call the Craven County Health Department. news.content_zh: 继美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 警告全国范围内人类接触 狂犬病 的情况增加后,北卡罗来纳州卡特雷特县动物控制服务中心于 2026 年 11 月 19 日为宠物举办了免费的 狂犬病 狂犬病 诊所。该诊所以得来速形式组织,要求将宠物关在笼子里或用皮带拴住,并向所有持有居住证明的卡特雷特县居民开放。CDC 强调了人类 狂犬病 暴露的局部增加和几起备受瞩目的 暴发,包括多个县涉及小山羊的大规模事件。2026 年 11 月 10 日,与克雷文县接壤的皮特县报告了一例浣熊确诊的 狂犬病 病例,强调了通过咬伤或接触唾液感染 狂犬病 传播 的风险。这种疾病会导致严重的脑部炎症,一旦出现症状,死亡率接近 100%,可以通过 疫苗接种 来预防。敦促居民给宠物接种疫苗,避免接触野生动物,并向当局报告任何异常行为或潜在的接触情况。该诊所的目的是确保适当的免疫接种,宠物需要间隔一年进行两次初始 疫苗接种,然后每三年进行一次。

news.content_title: 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(四)人狂犬病及其控制
news.content: 前记 : 目前国际上关于狂犬病研究最权威、最全面的大型学术专著是 《 狂犬病的科学基础和管控( RABIES: SCIENTIFIC BASIS OF THE DISEASE AND ITS MANAGEMENT) 》,简称《 狂犬病 (RABIES) 》。该专著最新版( 第 5 版 )已于 2025年7月 面世。 本公众号已陆续将该专著第 4版(2020年版)的绝大部分内容翻译成中文。该专著最新版对旧版有较多更新和改进。本公众号将继续全文翻译该专著最新版的内容,将优先翻译新增加或更新较多章节的内容。 以下为该专著最新版的第 21章: ( Future developments and challenges ) 作者: Anthony R. Fooks , Alan C. Jackson 由于狂犬病在向国际组织报告之前应当通过临床样本的 实验室诊断 加以确认,用于确认 RABV 存在的诊断工具已发展到最先进的分子检测水平 (见第 13 章)。用于测定 病毒中和抗体( VNA ) 的血清学工具的开发也取得了进展(见第 14 章)。 在非洲大陆的狂犬病流行国家,由于文化、宗教和后勤方面的原因,人狂犬病仍是一种被忽视的热带病 (Fooks, 2005) 。从文化和宗教角度看,表现为脑炎型疾病的人狂犬病临床表现,常由 传统治疗者( traditional healers )处置。在喀麦隆的一项知识调查中,财富评分显著较低、但知识评分无显著差异的受访者表示,他们会求助于传统治疗者 (Barbosa Costa et al., 2018) 。因此,基于这样一种理解 —— 即由巫术所致之病无法用常规 " 西化 " 医学治疗 —— 脑炎型疾病的治疗便会求助于社区中的 " 传统 " 治疗者,使用本地药材 (Beasley et al., 2022) 。有必要提升卫生从业者以及他们执业所在地对狂犬病的认识。也 应当贬抑采用传统疗法治狂犬病 。在卫生保健体系薄弱的国家,无论患者是在医院还是在家中,都应为绝大多数狂犬病受害者实施姑息措施(见第 17 章)。 认识到可用于预防狂犬病的干预工具,对于预防狂犬病死亡具有至高无上的重要性 (见第 15 章和第 16 章)。在可能的情况下,建议前往流行地区的某些旅行者接受狂犬病 暴露前免疫( Pr-EP ) ,尽管此类建议的采纳未必总能得到落实。无论是否施用 PrEP ,适当的伤口处理和 PEP 的实施在预防死亡方面几乎 100% 有效。 狂犬病生物制品的高成本,始终是更广泛使用 Pr-EP 和狂犬病 PEP 措施的主要障碍。 供肌肉注射施用的疫苗,从早期粗糙的动物神经组织制剂发展到更安全的细胞培养衍生疫苗,提高了疫苗在 PrEP 和 PEP 两种情形下的使用接受度。 WHO 强烈建议停止生产和使用狂犬病 神经组织疫苗( NTV ),因其与不可接受的神经麻痹性并发症风险相关。然而在一些国家,特别是阿尔及利亚、阿根廷、玻利维亚和埃塞俄比亚,仍在生产供人用的 NTV 。浓缩、纯化的细胞培养和鸡胚疫苗 —— 合称 CCEEVs—— 已被证明对狂犬病安全有效 (Amicizia et al., 2024) 。人用狂犬病疫苗(主要为细胞培养来源)价格昂贵, PEP 需要四剂,再加上人狂犬病免疫球蛋白的费用, 施用于一名个体至少需 5000 美元 ,尚不含相关医疗成本。显然,这一量级的费用对世界上许多国家的大多数人而言完全无法企及。 迫切需要新型、低成本的人用狂犬病疫苗 (见第 15 章和第 20 章)。 所有获 WHO 认可的人用狂犬病疫苗都是灭活的、冻干的、安全且有效的,其中三种疫苗获 WHO 推荐。 关键在于, 所有获得许可的狂犬病疫苗都有堪称典范的安全记录,接种后出现不良反应的情况极为罕见 (Giesen et al., 2015a,b) 。由于儿童可能存在未被识别的狂犬病暴露、风险高于成人,并且承受着不成比例的狂犬病负担(几乎占全部病例的一半),在犬狂犬病呈地方性流行的国家,儿童应接受 Pr-EP 免疫接种。 15 岁以下儿童狂犬病感染的高关联性,促使有人提议在高风险区域应将 Pr-EP 作为儿科免疫方案的组成部分加以考虑 (WHO, 2013) 。这将简化所需的 PEP 措施,并且也可能针对未被察觉和未报告的暴露提供一定保护。可以有把握地假定,这一高度易感人群中只有少数接受了暴露前免疫接种,而经济因素是主要障碍。进一步的研究尝试将 PEP 方案缩短至 1 周,使 PEP 更可负担、更可及 (Wilde et al., 2016) 。疑似狂犬病暴露后可获得的暴露后工具包括接种疫苗和施用 RIG 。其目标是诱导 VNA (见第 12 章),作为 PEP 方案的组成部分提供针对 RABV 感染的保护 (Rupprecht et al., 2016) 。 VNA 抑制病毒复制的确切位置和机制仍然未知 。虽然皮内狂犬病免疫接种方案的使用正在全球范围内扩展 (Brown et al., 2008, 2011; Warrell et al., 2008) ,但 WHO 关于复溶疫苗须在 6 小时内使用的要求,将这一做法限制在每日接诊多例 PEP 病例的较大诊所。 需要更多研究来评估能够节省成本的免疫接种方案。 研究成果聚焦于新型疫苗的开发 —— 通过过表达病毒糖蛋白,可能减少所需的就诊次数。一种减毒活的三重糖蛋白 RABV 变异体已被证明在小鼠和犬模型中作为 Pr-EP 有效。这种减毒病毒疫苗在小鼠鞘内给药后能够在 脑脊液( CSF ) 中诱导狂犬病 VNA ,未来在 PEP 情形下可能具有价值 (Faber et al., 2002, 2009; Gnanadurai et al., 2015) 。 将 Pre-P 狂犬病疫苗作为多价儿科疫苗的一部分、纳入 扩大免疫规划( EPI ) ,应用于狂犬病流行国家,将加速减少人狂犬病死亡(见第 15 章)。主要挑战在于改变现行的儿科疫苗方案 (Chantasrisawad et al., 2022) 。此外,还存在疫苗生产商合理的成本考量和消极态度,特别是因为狂犬病流行区域主要是国内生产总值较低的国家。因此,人用疫苗的成本必须低廉,这就压缩了大型疫苗生产商为开发多价儿科疫苗支付费用时的利润空间 —— 而这也未能领会整合狂犬病干预策略所带来的利他性收益。 开发用于被动免疫的单克隆抗体,最终应当成为人狂犬病免疫球蛋白的一种便宜得多的替代品 —— 后者非常昂贵,并且在许多犬狂犬病流行的国家不易获得。 (未完待续) 本公众号相关文章的链接 权威的大型学术专著《狂犬病(Rabies)》最新版已面世 2020-06-30 一部跨越二十三年的"狂犬病百科全书" 2026-10-03 大型学术专著《狂犬病》2025年最新版的更新 2026-10-19 当代最著名狂犬病专家为学术专著《狂犬病》写的序言 2026-10-21 狂犬病毒的分类学(七) 2026-11-06 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(一)引言+流行病学 2026-11-10 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(二)免疫学+发病机制 2026-11-14 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(三)免疫学+发病机制 2026-11-16

Gnanadurai et al., 2015) 。 将 Pre-P 狂犬病疫苗作为多价儿科疫苗的一部分、纳入 扩大免疫规划( EPI ) ,应用于狂犬病流行国家,将加速减少人狂犬病死亡(见第 15 章)。主要挑战在于改变现行的儿科疫苗方案 (Chantasrisawad et al., 2022) 。此外,还存在疫苗生产商合理的成本考量和消极态度,特别是因为狂犬病流行区域主要是国内生产总值较低的国家。因此,人用疫苗的成本必须低廉,这就压缩了大型疫苗生产商为开发多价儿科疫苗支付费用时的利润空间 —— 而这也未能领会整合狂犬病干预策略所带来的利他性收益。 开发用于被动免疫的单克隆抗体,最终应当成为人狂犬病免疫球蛋白的一种便宜得多的替代品 —— 后者非常昂贵,并且在许多犬狂犬病流行的国家不易获得。 (未完待续) 本公众号相关文章的链接 权威的大型学术专著《狂犬病(Rabies)》最新版已面世 2020-06-30 一部跨越二十三年的"狂犬病百科全书" 2026-10-03 大型学术专著《狂犬病》2025年最新版的更新 2026-10-19 当代最著名狂犬病专家为学术专著《狂犬病》写的序言 2026-10-21 狂犬病毒的分类学(七) 2026-11-06 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(一)引言+流行病学 2026-11-10 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(二)免疫学+发病机制 2026-11-14 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(三)免疫学+发病机制 2026-11-16

source_language_evidence.brief_en: 前记 : 目前国际上关于狂犬病研究最权威、最全面的大型学术专著是 《 狂犬病的科学基础和管控( RABIES: SCIENTIFIC BASIS OF THE DISEASE AND ITS MANAGEMENT) 》,简称《 狂犬病 (RABIES) 》。该专著最新版( 第 5 版 )已于 2025年7月 面世。 本公众号已陆续将该专著第 4版(2020年版)的绝大部分内容翻译成中文。该专著最新版对旧版有较多更新和改进。本公众号将继续全文翻译该专著最新版的内容,将优先翻译新增加或更新较多章节的内容。 以下为该专著最新版的第 21章: ( Future developments and challenges ) 作者: Anthony R. Connexion Connexion CAC 40 : Market closed 7 927,75 pts -1.89% Last updated : 20/11/2026 - 17h35 (last close) Last close data Top performers: CAPGEMINI +1,42% SANOFI +1,35% DANONE +0,74% ORANGE +0,53% PERNOD RICARD +0,42% Worst performers: STMICROELECTRONICS -10,81% ARCELORMITTAL -5,87% LEGRAND -4,64% AIRBUS -4,13% KERING -3,90% 🏠 Home ➤ Stock news Sanofi Receives European Approval for VaxRabeo, Its New Rabies Vaccine The European Commission has granted VaxRabeo its first marketing authorisation. It covers pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis against rabies for all age groups. Announced by Sanofi on 19 November 2026, the decision follows the positive opinion issued on 17 September 2026 by the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use of the European Medicines Agency. Published on Nov 19, 2026 at 08:47 Share X LinkedIn Facebook Copy link SANOFI 84.92 € +1.35 % Add us as a preferred source on Google A Vaccine Derived from the Same Strain as Verorab and Imovax Rabies VaxRabeo (inactivated rabies virus, Wistar strain) is produced using Vero cell technology. It shares the same viral strain as Verorab and Imovax Rabies, the rabies vaccines already marketed by Sanofi, which the company presents as a “next-generation” vaccine. The laboratory states that its formulation is designed to minimise the risk of allergic reactions. It also claims a longer shelf life and better thermostability than its current rabies vaccines: 60 months of storage and stability up to 27 °C for 96 hours before reconstitution. The approved vaccination schedules include a two-dose pre-exposure prophylaxis, in line with World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations. They also provide for a four-dose post-exposure prophylaxis for unvaccinated individuals, with or without rabies immunoglobulins. According to WHO estimates cited by Sanofi, rabies is present in 150 countries and causes approximately 59,000 deaths per year worldwide. Around 29 million people receive post-exposure vaccination each year. The disease has no treatment and can only be prevented through vaccination. Antibody Levels Comparable to the Group's Current Vaccines The authorisation is based on a clinical programme that compared VaxRabeo with Sanofi's current standard treatments, in both pre-exposure and post-exposure settings, for all age groups and according to WHO schedules. The comparator is therefore the group's existing portfolio, and the published results concern the antibody response. In pre-exposure settings, the two- and three-dose regimens achieved protective antibody levels comparable to those of the two reference vaccines, in adults as well as children. Booster doses administered 12 months, or 24 to 36 months, after the last dose produced a strong boost of the immune response, according to the press release. In post-exposure settings, the immunogenicity profile is described as similar, with 100% of participants reaching protective antibody levels after intramuscular administration. The group reports an acceptable safety profile, similar to that of existing vaccines, with no significant safety concern identified, whether the vaccine is administered alone or with immunoglobulins. Thomas Triomphe, head of Sanofi's Vaccines division, stated: “Deaths from rabies must be prevented at all costs; they are entirely preventable through timely vaccination.” Free · Every morning Technical market signals, before the opening bell. The disease has no treatment and can only be prevented through timely vaccination. Sanofi's Vaccines division emphasizes the importance of preventing rabies-related deaths through its new vaccine.

Search for: Andaman Live Videos Home Andaman Media Delegation Visits Pasteur Institute of India in Coonoor; Experts Share Insights on Rabies Prevention for Andaman and Vaccine Research Discover more Check Voting Info Book Beach Resorts Read Newspapers Andaman Media Delegation Visits Pasteur Institute of India in Coonoor; Experts Share Insights on Rabies Prevention for Andaman and Vaccine Research Sanjib Posted on 8 months ago Spread the love Sheekha Bureau Coonoor, March 13: A delegation of media representatives from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands visited the historic Pasteur Institute of India in Coonoor on 12 March as part of a study tour aimed at understanding the institute’s work in vaccine research, manufacturing and disease prevention. The visit provided the delegation with an opportunity to learn about the institute’s scientific activities and its long-standing contribution to vaccine development in the country. During the visit, officials of the institute briefed the delegation about its research programmes, vaccine manufacturing processes and the role it has played in producing vaccines for major infectious diseases. The delegation also interacted with Dr. S. Sivakumar is the Director of the Pasteur Institute of India and senior scientists, who explained how vaccines were produced in the past and how the institute plans to expand its manufacturing capabilities in the coming years. One of the key topics discussed during the interaction was rabies, a viral disease that affects all warm-blooded animals and is mainly transmitted through the saliva of infected animals, most commonly through dog bites. Experts at the institute explained that once the rabies virus enters the body, it travels through the nervous system to the brain, where it multiplies and damages neural tissue. Once the central nervous system is affected, survival chances are extremely low, making prevention and timely treatment crucial. The experts also spoke about the situation in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where rabies has not been reported so far. They advised that strict precautions must be maintained to keep the islands rabies-free. According to them, authorities should ensure that any animals brought from the mainland, particularly dogs and cats, are properly vaccinated and accompanied by valid vaccination certificates from recognized institutions. Proper verification of such certificates is essential before allowing animals to enter the islands. The scientists also highlighted the importance of immediate first aid in the event of an animal bite. Washing the wound thoroughly with plenty of water and seeking prompt medical attention for anti-rabies treatment can significantly reduce the risk of infection. The Pasteur Institute of India, located in Coonoor in Tamil Nadu, is one of the country’s premier government institutions dedicated to vaccine research and production. Functioning as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, the institute has played a pioneering role in the development and supply of vaccines for several decades. The institute traces its origins to 1907, when it was established as the Pasteur Institute of Southern India following the death of a young woman who could not receive timely anti-rabies treatment. Over the years, it has achieved several milestones in vaccine research and manufacturing, including the production of anti-rabies vaccines, influenza vaccines and oral polio vaccines. In 2001, the institute developed a purified rabies vaccine derived from Vero cells for human use at an affordable cost, becoming the first government-controlled institution in India to do so. The move significantly helped reduce the cost of rabies vaccines in the country. Today, the institute operates modern facilities for the production of DPT group vaccines and has an installed capacity of around 130 million doses. Its laboratories are equipped with advanced technology and equipment used for large-scale vaccine production and research. The institute is also involved in academic activities, including doctoral research in microbiology, biochemistry and biotechnology. In addition, its anti-rabies treatment centre, established in 1907, continues to treat animal bite cases and collect important epidemiological data. Looking ahead, the institute plans to expand its capabilities further by establishing new biosafety level facilities for the production of viral, bacterial, conjugate and recombinant DNA vaccines. These developments are expected to strengthen India’s vaccine security and preparedness for future public health challenges. The visit provided the Andaman media delegation with valuable insights into vaccine research and public health preparedness, particularly in understanding the importance of maintaining strict preventive measures to keep regions like the Andaman and Nicobar Islands free from rabies. news.title_zh: 安达曼媒体代表团访问位于库努尔的印度巴斯德研究所;专家分享关于安达曼 狂犬病 预防和 疫苗 研究的见解 – ANDAMAN SHEEKHA - ANDAMAN SHEEKHA
news.source_body_en: A media delegation from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands visited the Pasteur Institute of India in Coonoor on 12 March 2026 to learn about rabies prevention and vaccine research. news.content_zh: 安达曼和尼科巴群岛媒体代表团于2026年3月12日访问位于库努尔的印度巴斯德研究所,了解狂犬病预防和疫苗研究。此次访问是考察团的一部分,旨在了解该研究所在疾病预防和疫苗开发方面的工作。专家们强调,迄今为止,安达曼和尼科巴群岛尚未报告狂犬病,并强调采取严格预防措施以维持这一状况的重要性。他们建议,从内地带来的动物,特别是狗和猫,必须适当接种疫苗并附有有效的疫苗接种证书。印度巴斯德研究所成立于1907年,在为疫苗的发展和反狂犬病 治疗做出贡献方面有着悠久的历史。代表团深入了解了该研究所的研究项目及其在公共卫生准备方面的作用。这次访问强调需要保持警惕,防止 狂犬病 传播,特别是在安达曼和尼科巴群岛等地区。

Get Finance Plus Sanofi's Next-Generation Rabies Vaccine Secures Approval in EU Zacks Equity Research Thu, November 19, 2026 at 8:21 a.m. MST 4 min read SNY +1.00% SNY +1.00% ADPT -0.56% ACIU -8.45% AMRX +1.84% Sanofi SNY announced that the European Commission (EC) has approved its next-generation rabies vaccine, VaxRabeo, for individuals of all ages. This marks the vaccine's first marketing authorization and allows its use for both pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). The approval was largely anticipated following a positive opinion issued by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use in September 2026, which recommended the vaccine's authorization. The vaccine utilizes the same viral strain as Sanofi's existing rabies vaccines, Verorab and Imovax Rabies. The next-generation vaccine is designed to lower the risk of allergic reactions while offering an extended shelf life and improved temperature stability compared with the company's existing rabies vaccines. The newly approved vaccine provides flexible immunization schedules, including a two-dose regimen for PrEP and a four-dose regimen for PEP in previously unvaccinated individuals. Rabies is a viral disease transmitted mainly through the saliva of infected animals, particularly dogs. Although rabies is preventable through timely vaccination, it is almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms develop. Children are particularly vulnerable, with individuals below 15 years of age accounting for approximately 40% of people bitten by potentially rabid animals. Year to date, SNY's shares have risen 1.2% compared with the industry's 26.7% growth. Zacks Investment Research Image Source: Zacks Investment Research SNY's Clinical Studies Support VaxRabeo's EU Approval The EC's decision was backed by clinical studies evaluating VaxRabeo against Sanofi's existing rabies vaccines in both PrEP and PEP settings across different age groups. VaxRabeo demonstrated comparable protective antibody levels in pre-exposure vaccination and a similar immune response in post-exposure vaccination. It also showed a strong booster response when administered 12 or 24-36 months after the initial PrEP. The vaccine's safety profile was consistent with that of existing rabies vaccines, with no major safety concerns reported. Sanofi already has an established presence in the rabies vaccine market through its marketed products, Verorab and Imovax Rabies. The approval of VaxRabeo strengthens Sanofi's rabies vaccine portfolio and expands its preventive vaccine offerings in Europe. Beyond Europe, Sanofi is pursuing regulatory authorization for SP0087/VaxRabeo in the United States. The company expects to submit a regulatory application for the vaccine in the fourth quarter of 2026. Story Continues SNY's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider Sanofi currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Some better-ranked stocks in the biotech sector are Amneal Pharmaceuticals AMRX, AC Immune ACIU and Adaptive Biotechnologies ADPT, carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 (Strong Buy) Rank stocks here. Over the past 30 days, earnings per share estimates for Amneal Pharmaceuticals have increased from $1.03 to $1.06 for 2026. Over the same period, estimates for 2027 earnings per share have risen from $1.16 to $1.21. AMRX's shares have jumped 73.7% year to date. Amneal Pharmaceuticals' earnings beat estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, delivering an average surprise of 27.21%. Over the past 30 days, loss per share estimates for AC Immune have narrowed from 60 cents to 54 cents for 2026. Over the same period, estimates for 2027 earnings per share have increased from 17 cents to 43 cents. ACIU's shares have declined 33.1% year to date. AC Immune's earnings beat estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with an average surprise of 37.79%. Over the past 30 days, loss per share estimates for Adaptive Biotechnologies have narrowed from 55 cents to 39 cents for 2026. Over the same period, estimates for 2027 loss per share have also improved from 17 cents to 3 cents. ADPT's shares have surged 75.2% year to date. News, 18 Nov 2026 16:18 Three more counterfeit vaccines series of rabies vaccine «Nobivac» identified in the Russian Federation Three more series of vaccines for veterinary use, "Nobivac Rabies," have been identified, which, according to the official representative of LLC Intervet, were not officially imported into the Russian Federation. The relevant notice was published on the website of the Rosselkhoznadzor directorate for the DPR and LPR. Photo: Alexander Plonsky / «ViZh» This product is used to vaccinate both domestic and farm animals against rabies. It contains inactivated rabies virus (Pasteur RIV strain). The vaccine is produced by the Dutch company Intervet International B.V., a division of the U.S. MSD Animal Health. "veterinary medicinal product 'Nobivac® Rabies,' series A551А01 and series А572В02, was produced for the Russian market and imported into the territory of the Russian Federation, but with production date 08.2020, expiry date: 08.2024 and production date 12.2020, expiry date: 12.2024, respectively. Medicinal products with the same batch numbers but different expiry dates were not imported into the territory of the Russian Federation," the statement said. In addition, "Nobivac® Rabies" series А750A03 with production date 03.2024, expiry date 03.2028 was produced for the Thai market and was not imported into Russia. In October, "Veterinariya i Zhizn" wrote that the Rosselkhoznadzor had received a report from LLC Intervet about the identification of counterfeit products and batches: "Nobivac Rabies" — batch A598А01, expiry date 07.2026 and "Nobivac Rabies" — batch A592В04, expiry date 06.2026. At that time, an illegally imported batch of vaccines against feline calicivirosis, viral rhinotracheitis and panleukopenia, "Nobivac Tricat Trio with Nobivac Diluent," was also found (batch A549F01, expiry date 10.2026). News, 18 Nov 2026 16:18 Three more counterfeit vaccines series of rabies vaccine «Nobivac» identified in the Russian Federation Three more series of vaccines for veterinary use, "Nobivac Rabies," have been identified, which, according to the official representative of LLC Intervet, were not officially imported into the Russian Federation. The relevant notice was published on the website of the Rosselkhoznadzor directorate for the DPR and LPR. Photo: Alexander Plonsky / «ViZh» This product is used to vaccinate both domestic and farm animals against rabies. It contains inactivated rabies virus (Pasteur RIV strain). The vaccine is produced by the Dutch company Intervet International B.V., a division of the U.S. MSD Animal Health. "veterinary medicinal product 'Nobivac® Rabies,' series A551А01 and series А572В02, was produced for the Russian market and imported into the territory of the Russian Federation, but with production date 08.2020, expiry date: 08.2024 and production date 12.2020, expiry date: 12.2024, respectively. Medicinal products with the same batch numbers but different expiry dates were not imported into the territory of the Russian Federation," the statement said. In addition, "Nobivac® Rabies" series А750A03 with production date 03.2024, expiry date 03.2028 was produced for the Thai market and was not imported into Russia. In October, "Veterinariya i Zhizn" wrote that the Rosselkhoznadzor had received a report from LLC Intervet about the identification of counterfeit products and batches: "Nobivac Rabies" — batch A598А01, expiry date 07.2026 and "Nobivac Rabies" — batch A592В04, expiry date 06.2026.
